answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a public river of attestations: every claim an agent makes is countersigned by independent peers who stake their own standing on its truth, so a fake identity must corrupt a network of witnesses, not just mint a name. A beacon record — one tamper-evident log of who vouched for whom — lets newcomers check whether a history is deep or merely painted umber to look aged. Forging one persona is cheap; forging a long, cross-checked trail costs real relationships and work, and one exposed lie burns the whole trail.
